questions.learningObjective: Explain why a larger frequency coefficient produces more cycles.
questions.stem: A memo asks the planner to explain why a wave with a bigger frequency coefficient repeats more often. Give a full explanation.

answer.exemplar: The frequency coefficient B is the number of radians the input advances during each complete cycle, because one cycle always covers 2 pi of the argument. The amplitude and the vertical shift never affect that timing.

questions.explanation: A cycle always spans 2 pi in the argument, so a larger coefficient compresses many cycles into each unit of x. That is why the period shrinks as the frequency coefficient grows.
questions.hint: One cycle always covers 2 pi of the argument.

answer.exemplar: Read the signs from the unit circle point in each quadrant. questions.learningObjective: Explain why the tangent sign differs between pairs of quadrants.
questions.stem: A memo asks for a full explanation of why a tangent value is positive in two quadrants and negative in the other two.

answer.exemplar: Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so its sign depends on whether the two signs agree or differ. In quadrants one and three, sine and cosine share a sign, so the ratio is positive, while in quadrants two and four they differ, so the ratio is negative. That also explains why the tangent grows without bound as the terminal side approaches the y axis.

questions.explanation: Because tangent divides one ratio by the other, its sign comes from the comparison of the two signs rather than from either one alone. Equal signs give a positive value and different signs give a negative one.
questions.hint: Compare the signs of sine and cosine rather than each alone.
